slides.text: Lecture 7: Loops and Lists Introduction to Programming
Iteration Loops repeat a block of code A for loop visits each list element The loop variable changes every pass Accumulators collect a running total

Worked example def total_marks(scores):     total = 0     for s in scores:         if s < 0:             continue         total += s     return total  marks = [78, 91, -1, 64] print(total_marks(marks))
$ python marks.py 233 $ python -c "print(sum([78, 91, 64]))" 233 $ python marks.py --debug skipping invalid score -1 233
Iteration Lists are mutable sequences append adds an element at the end Index assignment replaces one element Aliasing shares one list object

Worked example def total_marks(scores):     total = 0     for s in scores:         if s < 0:             continue         total += s     return total  marks = [78, 91, -1, 64] print(total_marks(marks))
